text:
dmitri: seeing a spike in gRPC stream stalls for long-lived infer streams between gpu-pool-azb and gpu-pool-azc, started ~02:10 UTC. clients hit timeouts and then retries.
anya: ack. I can reproduce on a test job, streams hang after ~30s of steady tokens.
shiv: any packet drops or retransmit counters high?
dmitri: yes, on the sender node: lots of TX retransmits on the veth host end and kernel logs with 'IPV6: fragmentation needed' (we're IPv4 but saw PMTU ICMPs).
anya: ran tcpdump on the node-to-node link, noticed large segments and then no ACKs. here's the short pcap grep:
```
14:22:33.123456 IP 10.0.4.23.44312 > 10.0.5.78.61000: Flags [P.], seq 12345:23456, len 11111
14:22:33.124001 IP 10.0.4.23 > 10.0.5.78: frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1500)
```
anya: overlay MTU on calico is 1500 but host NICs are 9000. looks like encaps overhead pushes packets over 1500 and DF set is breaking PMTU.
shiv: are we using GSO/TSO/GRO? and RoCE/RDMA between GPU nodes?
dmitri: yes on these nodes we have kernel offloads enabled. also some nodes have RDMA enabled for NVLink RDMA fabric (RoCEv2) between GPUs for certain workloads.
anya: hypothesis: large gRPC chunks get GSO'd into huge host frames, then VXLAN/Geneve encaps makes them >1500 and DF prevents fragmentation; intermediate device sends ICMP frag-needed, but PMTU discovery isn't being honored in the veth/overlay bits, so packets drop and the gRPC stream stalls.
shiv: can we check `ethtool -k` and `ip link` quickly on a victim node?
dmitri: output from one node:
```
# ip link show dev eth0
3: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
# ethtool -k eth0 | egrep -i 'gso|tso|gro'
  tx-checksum-ip-generic: on
  tx-checksum-sctp: on
  tx-checksum-ipv4: on
  tx-checksum-udp: on
  tcp-segmentation-offload: on
  generic-segmentation-offload: on
  large-send-offload: on
  generic-receive-offload: on
```
anya: overlay interface mtu is 1450 in some nodes (we had different CNI configs during a rolling upgrade). that's the mismatch.
shiv: so some nodes negotiated different overlay MTUs -> path MTU different between AZs. that would explain intermittent stalls for cross-AZ streams.
ops-bot: notice: cluster-autoscaler drained node ip-10-0-5-12 for upgrade at 02:05 UTC in us-west-2c.
dmitri: that explains why only azc endpoints saw issues. older nodes still with 1500 overlay mtu, new ones 1450.
anya: quick mitigation: lower host NIC MTU to leave room for encaps: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 8950` or set CNI VXLAN/geneve mtu consistently (calico MTU=1440) and disable TSO/GSO on vxlan device.
shiv: disabling GSO on vxlan/encap might be safer short-term. command: `ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off tso off` (need to test).
dmitri: I pushed a debug daemonset to test nodes that sets vxlan gso off and sets `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` to allow better PMTU discovery.
anya: results: after disabling GSO on vxlan on two test nodes, stream stalls disappeared for that path; p95 latency returned to normal.
shiv: good. we should roll a conservative fix: update CNI config to set `mtu: 8900` cluster-wide and add node kick during maintenance window, plus option to disable GSO on vxlan in the CNI systemd prestart.
sre-oncall: impact summary: about 18% of GPU inference pods experienced timeouts for ~20 minutes across cross-AZ traffic. no data loss, but retries increased token cost and some jobs restarted, affecting SLAs.
dmitri: action items: 
- Anya: open a CNI change PR to unify overlay MTU to 8900 and include justification (encap overhead + GSO interactions).
- Shiv: add a host boot hook to disable VXLAN GSO on affected node images and a post-rollback plan.
- SRE-oncall: schedule a rolling restart for gpu node pool us-west-2c during maintenance window, notify customers.
- Ops-bot: create incident ticket INC-2026 and label `mtu-gso-gRPC` and attach pcap.
anya: also adding longer-term: evaluate RoCE/RDMA interactions with overlay (RoCE needs raw L2 or correct DCB config). if customers use RDMA for multi-node GPU, we should document dedicated networks or bypass overlay.
shiv: timeline: PR for CNI change by EOD, DR playbook draft, and test rollout to staging tomorrow.
dmitri: temporary rollback suggestion: if we see recurrence, set host eth0 mtu to 1500 for immediate mitigation and drain+replace nodes; that avoids overlay complexity but impacts jumbo benefits.
ops-bot: ticket INC-2026 created by dmitri at 02:58 UTC.
anya: note for the runbook: include commands we used and the pcap snippet, add checks `ss -tin` showing retransmits and `cat /proc/net/snmp | grep Segs` for segmentation errors.
sre-oncall: thumbs up. assign owners and I'll coordinate customer comms. :thumbsup:
shiv: will follow up with kernel bug tracker if we reproduce with GSO enabled + DF set; might be subtle kernel path that drops encaps ICMP handling.
dmitri: thanks all — rolling plan in PR. will post updates here during rollout.
